close_reason: Fixed by JMAP-r3pg.2 commit 99a8be3 — handle_calendar_event_get now passes get_args.time_zone.as_deref() to compute_utc_times. Verified by inline test calendar_event_get_time_zone_passed_to_compute_utc_times.
description:
src/event.rs:48 calls:

    backend.compute_utc_times(&account_id, &event, None).await

The third arg, tz_hint: Option<&str>, is the §5.7 'timeZone' argument from CalendarEvent/get. Per draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.7 (line 1437): 'timeZone: TimeZoneId (default "Etc/UTC") — The time zone to use when calculating the utcStart/utcEnd property of floating events.'

By passing None unconditionally, the handler drops the client-supplied timeZone and relies entirely on the event's own timeZone (or the backend's default fallback). For floating events (events with no timeZone property), this causes utcStart/utcEnd to be computed using a backend-default tz instead of the client's requested tz.

The CalendarsBackend::compute_utc_times default impl (src/backend.rs:171-178) returns (None, None) so the bug is invisible against the MockBackend — there are no tests of a real tz computation path. A backend that does support tz computation will silently use the wrong zone.

Note: this is the same root cause as JMAP-r3pg.2 (extra args dropped). Fixing JMAP-r3pg.2 by parsing the request and threading args through naturally fixes this site. Filing separately because the call site is a clean, easily-fixed atomic change even if the broader CalendarEventGetArgs struct work is deferred.

Fix: parse 'timeZone' from args before the handle_get call, then pass Some(&tz_str) to compute_utc_times instead of None. One-line fix once the value is in scope.
title: compute_utc_times always passes tz_hint: None — §5.7 timeZone arg dropped at the boundary
